title: 3.2.19 Lab: initials(first, last)
description: Write initials(first, last) so that it returns the first letter of each name joined into one string, using first[0]. Practice, not graded: the checks call your function.

steps.title: Write initials
steps.instructions: Write a function declaration called initials that takes two parameters, first and last.

steps.title: Take the first letter of each
steps.instructions: A string's first character is word[0] (2.2.19). So first[0] is the first name's letter and last[0] is the last name's.

steps.title: Join and return
steps.instructions: Join the two letters into one string with + and return it with return (3.2.11): initials("Ada", "Lovelace") gives "AL". Keep the letters exactly as they were typed.

steps.title: Check it
steps.instructions: Call initials with your own name and console.log the result.

requirements.title: initials is defined with two parameters
requirements.description: Code defines a function named initials with exactly two parameters. Help: 3.2.9 (Lab: findRectangleArea (multi-parameter))
requirements.hint: Write function initials(first, last) { ... } with exactly that name and two names between the parentheses.

requirements.title: initials hands back a value with return
requirements.description: initials contains a return statement. Help: 3.2.11 (Getting a Value Back with `return`)
requirements.hint: The line that produces the answer should start with return, not console.log.

requirements.title: initials returns the two first letters
requirements.description: initials(first, last) gives back the first letter of first followed by the first letter of last, as one string. Help: 2.2.19 (Walking Through a Word)
requirements.hint: initials must give back exactly two characters: the first letter of first, then the first letter of last. first[0] is the first letter of first. Check you did not return a whole name, swap the order, or print instead of returning.

cases.description: typed in lower case, so the letters stay lower case
